audit.why: Mirror settled it: difficulty turns on whether Steadfast Presence is live when he charges. Early lane is Poppy's, level 6 is Gragas's, late returns to Poppy on utility. 56.32% over 348 games supports the even 6/10 framing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five chart rows disagreed with the mirror and the packet: Level 1 read Skill, Level 2 read Poppy, Levels 4-5 read Skill, Level 6 read Skill, First item read Poppy.
audit.why: The mirror set the chart to Poppy / Skill / Poppy / Poppy / Gragas / Skill / Poppy as one atomic group, and the packet chart is identical. Poppy's own whys already read that way — whys[1] 'even until your E comes online', whys[4] 'Gragas spikes first at 6', whys[5] 'genuinely even' — so the side tokens were the outliers.
audit.corrected: phases[0,1,3,4,5].side and win[0,1,3,4,5] flipped as one group, with Poppy rows at 6/10, Skill rows 5/10 and Gragas's level 6 at 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (a) The page invents a Gragas 'pool' six times — 'pool-sustain (Q)', 'his pool can heal', 'his pool poke', 'pool damage reduction (W)', 'Q-pool the poke back', 'Fight in his Q puddle'. Gragas has no pool. Q is Barrel Roll, a cask that explodes and slows; his sustain is Happy Hour (P), which heals on skill use; W is Drunken Rage, an empowered auto plus damage reduction. (b) The decisive interaction was absent: Body Slam cancels Keeper's Verdict.
audit.why: Riot's own descriptions in champ-data/_kits/gragas.json carry no pool, no zone heal and no Q sustain. Poppy's R is flagged channel — any CC cancels it — and Body Slam is Gragas's stun.
audit.corrected: Every reachable 'pool' line rewritten to Barrel Roll / Happy Hour / Drunken Rage with real cooldowns; the channel cancel stated in whys[4], mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] mentions anti-heal generically but no lane-facing field told the player why.
audit.why: _missing flags Happy Hour as the sustain that decides extended trades, so Grievous Wounds timing matters.

audit.whatIsWrong: The early paragraph claimed Steadfast Presence 'stops the dash, slows and damages him'. W deals no damage.
audit.why: Riot's text: move speed, stop dashes, and on a stop the enemy is slowed and grounded. No damage component. The mirror agent corrected the same class of error from the other side.
audit.corrected: Damage claim removed; grounding stated instead. Also added Drunken Rage's auto-reset wind-up as the burst tell in dosFull[2].d.

edits.after: Happy Hour heals him every time he casts, so his Barrel Roll chip out-lasts your single ability until E comes online.

edits.after: Gragas spikes first at 6 — Explosive Cask knocks you back, and Body Slam (14s) cancels your Keeper's Verdict channel outright.

edits.before: Cheap tank components let you E-Q trade and tank his pool poke while your W keeps grounding his E engage.
edits.after: Cheap tank components let you E-Q trade and tank Barrel Roll while W keeps eating Body Slam every 14 seconds.

edits.before: Gragas wants to body-slam (E) into you, drop his pool (Q) and out-sustain your low base damage, so the lane is about denying that engage. Hold W to ground his Body Slam the moment he dashes in — it stops the dash, slows and damages him, and leaves him stranded next to a wall. That's your cue: E him into the wall for the stun and Q his max HP. At level 1 you're both weak, but by 3 your wall-stun combo out-trades anything his pool can heal.
edits.after: Gragas wants to Body Slam into you, sit on a Barrel Roll and out-sustain your low base damage through Happy Hour, so the lane is about denying that engage. Hold W to catch Body Slam the moment he charges — it stops the dash, slows him and leaves him grounded next to a wall. That's your cue: E him into the wall for the stun and Q his max HP. At 1 you're both weak, but by 3 the wall-stun beats what his passive heals back.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay yours on positioning — keep W up for his E and punish every body-slam with an E-into-wall stun and Q chunk. The catch is level 6: Gragas spikes harder than you do, because his R + E displacement and pool damage reduction (W) let him burst and disengage, while your R is a peel/displacement tool, not a kill button. Don't greed a trade into his ult window near your tower — bait his Body Slam, ground it with W, and reset.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours on positioning — keep W up for his E and punish every Body Slam with an E-into-wall stun and Q chunk. The catch is level 6: Gragas spikes harder, because Explosive Cask displaces you and Drunken Rage's damage reduction blunts your burst, while your R is peel, not a kill button — and Body Slam cancels that channel outright. Don't greed into his ult window near your tower — bait Body Slam, eat it with W, and reset.

edits.before: Force short trades levels 2-3 where your wall-stun combo beats his pool sustain
edits.after: Force short trades at 2-3, and buy Grievous Wounds before Happy Hour out-grinds you

edits.before: Land Body Slam (E) into you then W-shield the trade and Q-pool the poke back
edits.after: Land Body Slam, then Drunken Rage the reset auto and Barrel Roll the retreat

edits.before: Use his pool (Q) sustain to out-last your flat low base damage over time
edits.after: Lean on Happy Hour's per-cast heal to out-last your flat base damage

notes: phases[3].rating and phases[5].rating are proposed as no-op 6/10 and 5/10 so the chart lands as one complete atomic group; drop them if the applier rejects no-ops. dontsFull[1].t reads 'Fight in his Q puddle' — 21 characters, under the applier's 25-character skip threshold, so the fabricated 'puddle' cannot be removed by a normal edit. It needs a manual change to something like 'Stand in the Barrel Roll blast'. Separately: Body Slam carries no 'dash' flag in champ-data/_kits/gragas.json even though Riot's text is 'charges to a location' and the whole matchup is built on Steadfast Presence stopping it. The mirror agent treated it as a dash from the Gragas side, so I kept that reading; the missing flag looks like a parse gap rather than a design fact.
